title: Paffett wins Hockenheim opener from sixth on the grid
dek: Gary Paffett won the first DTM race of the new era from sixth on the grid, 4.709 seconds clear of fellow Mercedes driver Jamie Green, after pole-sitter Mattias Ekström slipped to third.

chapters.title: A new DTM era, and BMW is back
text: The 2012 DTM season opened at the Hockenheimring on Sunday 29 April with all-new cars and a third manufacturer on the grid. BMW returned to the series after a gap of two decades with the M3 DTM, joining the Audi A5 DTM and the Mercedes AMG C-Coupé. The 22-car field was split eight Audis, eight Mercedes and six BMWs, and the technical rules had been rewritten to cut costs, increase safety and reduce aerodynamic influence in the hope of closer racing.

There were other changes too. Refuelling was banned and each driver had to make two mandatory tyre stops, and the championship adopted a Formula One-style scale of 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1 for the first ten finishers. For Audi, Mattias Ekström, the 2011 runner-up, was keen to give the new car a flying start and expected the competition to be tougher than ever. The number 1 had also changed sides: Martin Tomczyk, the defending champion, had moved from Audi to BMW Team RMG and said that everybody now wanted to take the number back from him.

BMW's hopes were mostly a matter of guesswork. Andy Priaulx, a three-time World Touring Car champion, was making his DTM debut for BMW Team RBM, and Bruno Spengler had topped Saturday morning's final practice, which hinted that the newcomers would not simply be making up the numbers.

chapters.title: Ekström takes pole as BMW reaches the second row
text: Qualifying on Saturday was split into four segments. The slowest six drivers were eliminated in each of the first three, and the surviving four met in a one-lap shoot-out for pole. Joey Hand produced the drama of Q1, jumping from 19th to seventh on his final lap and sending Miguel Molina out. Molina, David Coulthard, Augusto Farfus, Roberto Merhi, Susie Wolff and Rahel Frey were all eliminated at that stage. In Q2 Priaulx pushed Ralf Schumacher out of the top ten after the flag, and Adrien Tambay outqualified the Audis of Filipe Albuquerque and Molina.

Q4 belonged to Ekström. His 1:34.680 for Abt Sportsline was a clean lap, while the other three finalists all made mistakes. Green, last to go after setting the pace in Q3, locked his brakes at Turn 2 and ended up 0.215 seconds slower in second. Dirk Werner ran wide at the Spitzkehre and Edoardo Mortara ran wide at the Nordkurve, but Werner still took third on the grid and left Audi, Mercedes and BMW in the top three places.

Mike Rockenfeller was fifth, ahead of Gary Paffett, who had to settle for sixth on 1:34.287 in Q3. Priaulx was seventh, Timo Scheider eighth, Spengler ninth and Tomczyk tenth, so four of the six BMWs reached the top ten. Christian Vietoris, who made an error in Q2, lined up 15th, and Farfus was down in 19th.

chapters.title: Chaos at the Spitzkehre, Ekström runs wide
text: The opening laps cost several of the favourites their races. Werner got away slowly from third and dropped back, and on lap two Ralf Schumacher braked too late for the Spitzkehre hairpin and hit him. The same incident damaged Spengler's BMW, which lost its engine cover, and his race was over on the third lap, as was Tambay's after he too was caught up in the incident. Tomczyk's BMW was damaged in several collisions and he stopped on lap four, while Scheider's Audi was out after 13.

At the front the race was changing shape. Paffett passed Werner and Rockenfeller on the first lap, then made a well-judged move on Mortara's Rosberg Audi shortly afterwards to take third. Ekström ran wide at Turn 2, allowing Green past on about lap five, and Paffett followed through at the exit of the hairpin shortly afterwards. Green led from that point, with Paffett close behind him and the Audis already beginning to lose touch.

chapters.title: Paffett jumps Green in the pit lane
text: The first of the two mandatory stops decided the race. Green came in first and Paffett stayed out for one more lap, then produced a quick in-lap and a clean stop. The two Mercedes left the pit lane side by side, ran together through Turn 2 and all the way down the main straight, and at the Spitzkehre Paffett had the inside line and the better braking to take the lead. Green said afterwards that Paffett's stop had been faster than his own.

From there Paffett eased away from Green. Elsewhere the second round of stops brought trouble for Farfus. He missed his pit box, went around again and was penalised for speeding in the pit lane on the second attempt, and he finished 15th. Paffett was first of the leaders to make his second stop, rejoined about three seconds ahead of Green, and Ekström, who was losing around three tenths a lap, was far enough behind that the fight for the podium was over.

chapters.title: Paffett by 4.7 seconds, Vietoris charges to fourth
text: Paffett took the chequered flag after 40 laps in 1:04:37.615, 4.709 seconds ahead of Green. Green had fresher tyres in the closing stages and was quicker, but the gap was too big and the laps too few. He set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:34.901 on lap 31, and settled for second. Ekström finished third, 19.434 seconds behind the winner.

Behind them Vietoris produced the drive of the day, climbing from 15th on the grid to fourth for Mercedes and passing Rockenfeller's Phoenix Audi with five laps to go. Rockenfeller took fifth, 27.834 seconds back. Priaulx closed a gap of around four seconds to just 0.601 at the flag but could not get past, and took sixth, the best result for BMW. Schumacher recovered to seventh, ahead of Coulthard in eighth and Molina in ninth, and Albuquerque took the final point in tenth. Eighteen cars were classified and four retired.

chapters.title: Mercedes leads after a turbulent opener
text: Paffett called it a fantastic start to the new DTM era and said the battle with Green had been exciting and always fair. After a difficult 2011 he felt he had found his way back to the top step of the podium. Green, who passed Ekström early on, said his set-up had been perfect, and he was satisfied with second place and with a one-two for Mercedes. HWA's Vietoris said he had never dreamt after qualifying that he could climb from 15th to fourth, and praised his pit crew. Coulthard was pleased with eighth after a winter of uncertainty and said it showed where the team stood against its rivals. Five Mercedes finished in the top eight.

Ekström, the pole-sitter, admitted that third place was not what he wanted. He said the Audi was not quick enough on the day and that his mistake had made things worse, though he promised the team would come back. For BMW the result was mixed. Priaulx, as the only one of the six cars to complete the distance without being involved in a major incident, took the first points of the comeback and said he would have accepted sixth place before the weekend. Jens Marquardt said he was very happy with the return overall. Merhi was damaged in a collision early on and was classified 18th, two laps down.

Spengler, Tambay and Tomczyk all failed to score, while Hand, Farfus and Werner finished 13th, 15th and 17th. Werner had started third and dropped to 17th, a lap down. Under the new points scale Paffett led the championship on 25 points, ahead of Green on 18, Ekström on 15, Vietoris on 12, Rockenfeller on 10 and Priaulx on eight.

About 71,000 watched the race on Sunday and 142,000 attended over the weekend. Audi's Wolfgang Ullrich described the start of the new era as fabulous for the fans but said his team now needed to turn perfect qualifying into a win. There was little time to reflect: the series moved on to the Lausitzring for round two just one week later, on Sunday 6 May, with Mercedes leading the championship and BMW eager to repair its cars and show that Priaulx's result was no fluke.

facts.v: Gary Paffett started sixth and won by 4.709 seconds from Jamie Green, with pole-sitter Mattias Ekström third.
